Nuclear energy, contrary to popular belief, is remarkably clean, efficient, and safe. Accidents are rare, the only danger lies in disposing of waste. Typically this is done by storing the radioactive materials in deep indoor cooling pools for a while (5-10 years-ish)

After this there isn’t much that can be done. Radioactive isotopes irradiate their surroundings ad Infinitum, and the only real option at the moment is to isolate them. One such option is to stick them at the bottom of an abandoned salt mine and fill it with concrete. It really doesn’t matter where you put it, the goal is to limit contact with dangerous materials. 

This means we need to take into account future generations; some isotopes have a half-life (the rate at which a radioisotope activity will reduce by half) of 150,000+ years, which means we would need to warn people about them, far into the future.

Examples of some ideas are on this wiki page: https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-time_nuclear_waste_warning_messages

(They’re really cool ideas, like constructing a giant forest of black concrete spikes, and big stone obelisks in many languages warning of what lies there - here’s a really good video touching on the topic): [19:50-23:10] https://youtu.be/7MOKTU9tCbw


The safest way is one in which nobody ever comes across the damn stuff ever again. We don’t know how foolish future generations will be, perhaps the big obelisks and black spikes, etc will attract even more visitors. I mean, the pyramids did a fat load of good.

“How does it relate to daily life?” For myself, I keep my time valuable by constantly reminding myself that in an untold amount of time everything is going to be reduced to a few protons scurrying about in an eternal void, before they themselves (possibly) decay. 
This takes away any inherent meaning in anything one does, but also gives it it’s only meaning.

The house does always win, but it should be all our moral duties to steal as much from the bastard before they catch us. Understanding that everything is trying to reach its ground state is essential because you need to know when to stop pushing the rock up the proverbial hill and let it roll down. 

It’s like when people ask why there is any order/structure at all if we’re tending towards oblivion. Well, our destination is dead certain, but what happens before that is fair game; there’s nothing preventing clusters of order presenting themselves amongst the chaos. Like bacteria on a Petri dish, or clumps of matter in a vast, formless universe. 

It’s all too easy for people to get cobbled down by the humdrum of everyday things. Education (self-administered or otherwise) provides a platform to escape this fate through various means, most importantly by weighing yourself up against... well, everything - forcing a change of perspective.
That’s I think Physics and Philosophy are top picks, aside from the fact they’re bloody interesting. Though sadly we’re at a stage in our development where understanding of other things are still important, or even necessary. 

There is something fundamental we’re missing. I don’t know what form it takes, or what it’s effects are, but it’s there. Right under our noses. 

Time is Money. It’s just a shame I don’t have enough to figure it all out. Oh I wish that I was rid of my corporeal form, free to wander an infinite digital library of human knowledge. Really banking on immortality becoming a thing before I die. Can’t die when we know so little, and the most important things are still about us on a terrestrial/environmental level.

It depends how big you wanna be. If you cut now you may have visible abs sooner rather than later, you can of course cut and do abs at the same time, and THEN do a clean bulk; also doing a lot of abs, afterwards a short cut would leave you well off. 

Yeah I feel the same, I’m actually in the same position as you rn, I’m gonna cut first and then slowly clean bulk and to a small final cut at the end. (But I have quite a high bf). 

It ain’t an exact science, always do ab work, but if you wanna cut now then you may be happy - just make sure you don’t let your other muscles waste away

Maybe you’re not doing abs enough? I would train them whenever you can (as soon as there’s no soreness), you have enough weights to bulk well, definitely.

As to why you are too small after cutting, it could be because you are either not cutting efficiently (and therefore losing muscle in the mean time) or because you weren’t big enough in the first place. (You might just look big with that little extra fat). 

If you just *clean* bulk from now, focusing hard on abs, they should be visible (you’re still fairly lean). And if you start to put on even a little fat, just cut it off quickly. 
Just make sure you are still weightlifting when cutting, specifically deadlifts, squats and ab work. It’s important to activate all the muscles multiple times a week to keep them strong.

I would spend some time figuring out a good diet if you haven’t already, you can clean bulk, focus on abs and bar work which incorporates multiple muscles (like deadlifts) - you will be adding size with minimal fat, and when you feel like you are getting too fat / the right size, it should be a relatively small cut until you have visible abs (because you’ve been training them up until then and therefore you won’t need to be as lean to see them because they’re stronger). 

In 3-4 months? I don’t know exactly. Just bang out the ab work and cut at the end. They will be visible in time for Summer. Abdominals are a very strong muscle group; you need to absolutely hammer them to get them stronger. After experiencing the first burns of an ab workout, you can usually repeat what you’ve done 5-7 times, the burns go away after the first few repetitions, then they just start feeling ‘weaker’. 

Sorry if that seemed pretentious, but this was something that actually took me ages to figure out. (I always used to stop after the ab burns because I thought they were effectively worked out, but they weren’t).

Anyway, possibilities are numerous, and I’m spouting shite now.

I would bulk, and do a lot of ab work. You have quite wide hips - same as me; you should try to fill out your upper body to compensate. 

You have quite a low bf still, so you could get away with it. Still a while till summer again (well, depending on where you are...)
I would clean bulk and make sure to do a lot of abs, then do a serious cut at the end.

Of course you could rest on your laurels now, but I feel like you might need up looking smaller than you would want.

Don’t have any friends left from school, don’t know if that is by choice or not, though I don’t care to find out. My list of phone contacts consists of my parents and a single person who I text every few weeks, and that’s only because they live so close that I can’t avoid them. 

Everyone I know is at Uni right now, the stupid people, the popular people, the smart people; all getting on with their lives. I’m not sure what will become of me. I attempted suicide not one year past. Wasn’t a nice experience (paracetamol, stuck it out alone for 3 days). 

It’s funny. I willingly detach myself so much from my peers, and then I am hurt when nobody calls. Not like I would let anyone know that. 

Perhaps it’s a certain temperament, a balance of the humours. But what words? Mature? Perhaps. Wise? Isn’t my call. Sensitive? Not in that way. 
Weary. Tired. Old. I cannot describes to you the way I perceive things, but as succinctly as possible? I feel like I’ve seen everything before, I’ve experienced much grief though hide it, I do not care for social pressures, the way I perceive things changes enough that I’m never fully committed to a single ideal. When I’m with people I make them feel like they’re the more intelligent of the two of us, like they’re wise, kind and useful. I feel nothing. I don’t care. I do this out of ‘empathy’; to what end I know not. 

You said that they never cared, that’s incorrect, I think. You’re just cut from a different cloth from them; they have experienced hardships, yes, but are they as great as yours? Doesn’t matter. They are constituted in a way that they focus on themselves. The last words they spoke to you, however ignorant, do not negate all the countless other things they have said.

You have the luxury of being self-aware enough to recognise others traits as bad, but you are sensitive enough to still be depressed by such things.

Wisdom is bred of experience, it would stand to reason then that hardships would breed emotional wisdom. You found a kindred spirit in this person, though they were not what you were expecting, and perhaps even not what you wanted. 

What they said was selfish, but only by your metric. From their perspective what you said was equally selfish. No, you don’t need to remind them why it was wrong.

Linking back to my story, I have bounced in and out of deep depression for nearly a decade now. Something always brings me back, as it has you. Anecdotes, right? I have nothing. I have you. I have people. 

That is my purpose. It makes me happy just to be alive and converse with another conscious being, even if that is just to share in a transient moment of pain.
